'''Vito Latora''' is an Italian physicist, currently Professor in Applied Mathematics (Chair of Complex Systems) at the School of Mathematical Sciences of the [[Queen Mary University]] of London. He is known for his works on [[complex systems]], in particular on the structure and dynamics of [[complex networks]].

== Career ==

Latora received a PhD in physics from the [[University of Catania]] in Italy for a thesis in the field of theoretical [[nuclear physics]] entitled "''Multifragmentation, [[phase transition]]s and critical chaos in hot nuclei''". He conducted postdoctoral research at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) in the group of [[:de:Michel Baranger|Michel Baranger]], in the group of [[Eric J. Heller|Eric Heller]]  at [[Harvard University]], and at [[Paris University XI]]. After his postdoctoral period, he joined the department of Physics of the University of Catania as an assistant professor in 2002. Since 2012, Vito Latora is Full Professor in Applied Mathematics (chair in Complex Systems) at the [[Queen Mary University of London|Queen Mary University]] of London.<ref name="qmul">{{cite web |title=People - School of Mathematical Sciences |website=[[Queen Mary University of London]] |url=https://www.qmul.ac.uk/maths/people/ |access-date=April 11, 2014 }}</ref>

== Research ==

After initial work in the field of [[Nuclear physics|theoretical nuclear physics]], his scientific contributions have focused on statistical physics, complex systems and, especially, complex networks. Noteworthy, he has developed together with [[Massimo Marchiori]] the so-called "''network efficiency''",<ref name="vito_eff_prl">{{cite journal | last1 = Latora | first1 = V. | last2 = Marchiori | first2 = M. | year = 2001 | title = Efficient Behavior of Small-World Networks | journal = Physical Review Letters | volume = 87 | issue = 19| article-number = 198701 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.87.198701 | pmid = 11690461 | bibcode=2001PhRvL..87s8701L| arxiv = cond-mat/0101396 | s2cid = 15457305 }}</ref><ref name="vito_eff_2">Centrality [[Centrality#cite note-14]], "Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia". Retrieved April 11, 2014.</ref> a topological measure that accounts for the capability of a system to deliver information, or goods, spending the least amount of resources. He is also well known for his works on spatial systems and in particular on urban street networks.<ref name="art_cities1">Matteo Bradicich, [http://scienza.studionews24.com/metamorfosi-urbana-ultimo-secolo-esplorazione-densificazione/ "La metamorfosi urbana dell'ultimo secolo: Esplorazione e Densificazione"], "scienza.studionews24.com", (2012-03-09).</ref><ref name="art_cities2">Sarah Fecht, [http://www.scientificamerican.com/article/grid-unlocked-how-street/ "Grid Unlocked: How Street Networks Evolve as Cities Grow"], "Scientificamerican.com", (2012-04-06).</ref><ref name="art_cities3">[http://www.lescienze.it/news/2012/03/03/news/crescente_urbanizzazione_mondiale_fattori_determinanti_strade_milano_groane-884848/ "Le leggi nascoste che guidano la crescita urbana"], "Le Scienze", (2012-03-03).</ref> His other contributions span a wide range of subjects ranging from [[statistical mechanics]], to [[neuroscience]], and [[social science]].<ref name="symbol1">Lisa Zyga, [http://phys.org/news204800347.html "Scientists develop new way to decipher hidden messages in symbols"], "PhysOrg.com", (2010-09-27).</ref><ref name="symbol2">[http://www.physicscentral.com/explore/multimedia/podcast.cfm?uid=20101027115243 "The Twitter Method"], "physicscentral.com", (2012-07-11).</ref><ref name="neuro1">[https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2013/05/130503132954.htm "Mathematicians help unlock brain function"], "sciencedaily.com", (2013-05-03).</ref>

== Awards ==

In 2008, Latora has been awarded with the "[[:it:Giovan Pietro Grimaldi|Giovan Pietro Grimaldi]] Prize".<ref name="premio2">[http://www.fondazionegrimaldi.it/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=24:terza-edizione-2008&catid=5:premio-giovan-pietro-grimaldi-per-la-fisica&Itemid=14 Terza edizione Premio Giovan Pietro Grimaldi], "fondazionegrimaldi.it", (2008-10-25).</ref><ref name="premio3">Università di Catania, [http://www.agendabda.unict.it/open_page.php?sez=articolo&id=1974 "Premio Giovan Pietro Grimaldi"], "agendabda.unict.it", (2008-10-25).</ref><ref name="premio1">Radio TRM, [http://www.radiortm.it/2008/10/25/modica-cerimonia-di-consegna-del-premio-giovan-pietro-grimaldi-al-fisico-vito-latora-che-studia-le-reti-complesse-con-ottimi-risultati/ "Modica: Cerimonia di consegna del premio Giovan Pietro Grimaldi Al fisico Vito Latora che studia le reti complesse"], "radiortm.it", (2008-10-25).</ref> The motivation of the prize was: "''For his works on the structure and dynamics of complex networks''".

In 2021, Latora has been nominated fellow of the [https://netscisociety.net/ Network Science Society] with the following citation: "''For seminal work on the structure and dynamics of temporal, multilayer, and higher-order networks, and innovative applications of network science to other disciplines, including neuroscience and urban design.''"<ref name="premio4">{{cite web |title=Award & Prizes - List of Network Science Society fellows |url=https://netscisociety.net/award-prizes/society-fellows |access-date=2021-07-13 }}</ref>

In 2026, Latora has been nominated fellow of the [https://www.aps.org/ American Physical Society] with the following citation: "''For pioneering contributions to the statistical physics of complex networks, including foundational work on network efficiency, cascading failures, multilayer networks, and higher-order interactions.''" <ref name="premio5">{{cite web | title=APS Fellowship recipients -- Division of Statistical and Nonlinear Physics | url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?t=Division%20of%20Statistical%20and%20Nonlinear%20Physics%20Fellowship&af=true | access-date=2026-10-13}}</ref>
